questions.q: What was 'the first time' for Jarvis and his wife at the Parkwold Church service?
choices: The first time they had been to a funeral
The first time they had sat in a church with people who were not white
The first time they had heard the Bishop
The first time they had left the farm
questions.explain: White, black, coloured and Indian people came, and the church was too small for them all.

questions.q: What did the Bishop say in his address?
choices: That the killer must hang
That men do not understand the riddle of why such a young man of promise was cut off — and he spoke of a life devoted to South Africa 'of love that cast out fear'
That the family should leave the country
Nothing of substance
questions.explain: Jarvis feels pride 'in the stranger who had been his son.'

questions.q: What 'first time' does Jarvis experience at the funeral itself?
choices: The first time he had cried in public
The first time he had ever shaken hands with black people
The first time he had flown
The first time he had missed the ploughing
questions.explain: 'The black people — yes, the black people also' — shook hands with him.

questions.q: How does Harrison say the people of Johannesburg feel about crime at that moment?
choices: Unconcerned
'Scared stiff' — they barricade their houses at night
Confident the police have it in hand
Sympathetic to the criminals
questions.explain: He cites the Phillipsons, robbed and beaten three doors down.

questions.q: What does Harrison say about a threatened mine strike?
choices: It will not happen
The miners want ten shillings a day (they get about three shillings a shift), and 'if mining costs go up much more there won't be any mines'
The mines have already agreed to the demand
It is only a rumour
questions.explain: Harrison argues the whole country depends on the mines.

questions.q: How did Arthur respond, according to Harrison, when asked about the robbery of the Phillipsons?
choices: He demanded harsher sentences
He 'reckoned we were to blame somehow'
He said nothing
He blamed the police
questions.explain: Harrison couldn't always follow Arthur but felt 'he had a kind of sincerity.'

questions.q: What does John Harrison quietly tell Jarvis about his father's use of the word 'Afrikaners'?
choices: That his father is an Afrikaner himself
That when his father says 'Afrikaners' he means 'Nationalists' — Arthur was always telling him that
That his father hates all Afrikaners
Nothing about it at all
questions.explain: 'And father would agree too, but he just doesn't seem able to remember.'

questions.q: What does Jarvis ask John Harrison to show him?
choices: Arthur's grave
The Boys' Club in Gladiolus Street, Claremont
The mine compounds
The non-European Hospital
questions.explain: 'It was our Club. Arthur's and mine,' John says.

questions.q: What does Jarvis say to Harrison about talking of his son?
choices: That he cannot bear to
That it does him good — 'I'm not a man to sit and talk about death by the hour', but hearing about Arthur's work helps
That Harrison should stop
That it is a private matter
questions.explain: He wishes he could have heard Arthur argue with Harrison.

questions.q: What does the chapter suggest Jarvis is slowly doing as he listens?
choices: Planning revenge
Coming to know, and to understand, a son who had become a stranger to him
Deciding to sell the farm
Losing interest in the case
questions.explain: The theme of Book Two: Jarvis's education by his dead son's words and example.
